name: Bodyweight Split Squat
summary: A stationary lower-body compound movement performed in a split stance to build unilateral leg strength and stability.

setup: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot backward into a comfortable split stance, elevating the rear heel so your weight rests on the ball of the back foot.
Distribute your weight primarily through the front foot and maintain an upright torso with hands on your hips or clasped at your chest.
steps: Lower your hips straight down by bending both knees simultaneously until your back knee is hovering just above the floor.
Pause briefly at the bottom, ensuring your front thigh is nearly parallel to the floor.
Drive through the midfoot and heel of your front foot to extend both knees and return to the starting position without moving your feet.
Complete the prescribed repetitions, then switch leg positions.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower your body down, and exhale forcefully as you press back up to the starting position.

common_faults.fault: Positioning feet in a straight line like on a tightrope, compromising lateral balance.
common_faults.correction: Keep feet roughly hip-width apart in terms of width while stepping back into the split.

common_faults.fault: Shifting excessively forward onto the front toes, lifting the front heel off the floor.
common_faults.correction: Lengthen your split stance slightly and focus on lowering your hips straight down while keeping the front heel planted.

common_faults.fault: Front knee caving inward during the descent or ascent.
common_faults.correction: Actively track the front knee outward in line with the middle toes.

precautions: Use a wall or sturdy support for balance if unilateral stability is limited.
